findings.title: register_route can create duplicate in-memory routes
findings.summary: register_route always appends to self.routes while save_route upserts the DB. Re-registering a route_id can produce duplicate candidates until restart.

findings.remediation: Use RouteRegistry keyed by route_id and replace/update in-memory projection transactionally.

findings.title: First-use posterior initialization can overwrite concurrent learning
findings.summary: get() calls _upsert with ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE. A concurrent initializer can replace a posterior that another worker just updated.
findings.invariant: The implementation must satisfy the stated trust/consistency property on the exact reviewed subject.

evidence.detail: get() calls _upsert with ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE. A concurrent initializer can replace a posterior that another worker just updated.

findings.remediation: Initialize with INSERT OR IGNORE; never overwrite an existing posterior from a prior-read path.

findings.title: Cemetery re-bury still deletes the previous structured episode

evidence.detail: When an entry is REVIVED, bury deletes the old cemetery row before inserting the new one, so historical burial assumptions are not preserved in the structured table.

findings.remediation: Make cemetery episodes append-only and derive current burial status separately.

findings.title: Migration application and version/hash recording are not atomic

findings.remediation: Implement one all-or-nothing migration transaction strategy and test a deliberately failing multi-statement migration.

findings.title: Legacy applied migrations with NULL content_hash remain outside drift protection

findings.remediation: Add an explicit migration baseline process: compare schema fingerprint, record accepted historical hashes once, then require non-null digest for every applied version.

findings.title: Two verification runners own incompatible receipt formats
findings.summary: CLI writes core VerificationRunner run directories; BuildCertificateBuilder reads proof/runner receipts.jsonl. They are separate sources of verification truth.

findings.title: CI Build Certificate is not bound to the pytest/lint/type-check gates
findings.summary: CI executes pytest/ruff/pyright directly, then runs one CLI smoke through the other verification runner. build_certificate.py reads qdw.proof receipts, so the preceding gates are not the certificate's mandatory receipt set.
findings.invariant: The implementation must satisfy the stated trust/consistency property on the exact reviewed subject.

evidence.detail: CI executes pytest/ruff/pyright directly, then runs one CLI smoke through the other verification runner. build_certificate.py reads qdw.proof receipts, so the preceding gates are not the certificate's mandatory receipt set.

findings.remediation: Execute a frozen release VerificationPlan through one VerificationService and issue from that run ID.

findings.title: Build certificate derives its requirements from whatever receipts happened to exist
findings.summary: The script chooses the most common task_id, converts observed receipt argv into required_commands, and uses acceptance_spec_hash='ci_pipeline'. The acceptance criteria are therefore not frozen before execution.
findings.invariant: The implementation must satisfy the stated trust/consistency property on the exact reviewed subject.

evidence.detail: The script chooses the most common task_id, converts observed receipt argv into required_commands, and uses acceptance_spec_hash='ci_pipeline'. The acceptance criteria are therefore not frozen before execution.

findings.remediation: Require an explicit VerificationPlan/AcceptanceSpec path and content hash. Required commands come from the plan, never from observed receipts.

findings.title: Negative-test semantics are inverted
findings.summary: required_negative_tests are considered successful only when the process exits nonzero. A proper pytest adversarial test should exit 0 while asserting that malicious input was rejected.
findings.invariant: The implementation must satisfy the stated trust/consistency property on the exact reviewed subject.

evidence.detail: required_negative_tests are considered successful only when the process exits nonzero. A proper pytest adversarial test should exit 0 while asserting that malicious input was rejected.

findings.remediation: Model attacks separately: the test command must PASS and the AttackResult records that the bad action was rejected for the expected reason.

findings.title: Certificate issuance does not enforce one clean exact Git subject across receipts
findings.summary: Receipt lookup is by argv/task_id; certificate git_sha comes from receipts[0]. It does not reject mixed SHAs, dirty receipts, or different working directories/environments.
findings.invariant: The implementation must satisfy the stated trust/consistency property on the exact reviewed subject.

evidence.detail: Receipt lookup is by argv/task_id; certificate git_sha comes from receipts[0]. It does not reject mixed SHAs, dirty receipts, or different working directories/environments.

findings.remediation: Bind VerificationRun to one subject SHA/dirty=false; every mandatory receipt must match run_id, SHA, cwd and plan hash.

findings.title: Certificate revalidation reruns changed code instead of validating the original evidence set
findings.summary: verify_certificate re-executes commands in cert.get('cwd','.'), but cwd is not stored in the certificate. It does not validate the actual acceptance-spec file and can verify a later checkout rather than the certified subject.
findings.invariant: The implementation must satisfy the stated trust/consistency property on the exact reviewed subject.

evidence.detail: verify_certificate re-executes commands in cert.get('cwd','.'), but cwd is not stored in the certificate. It does not validate the actual acceptance-spec file and can verify a later checkout rather than the certified subject.

findings.remediation: Separate evidence verification from optional replay. Verify immutable receipts/artifacts/spec/SHA first; replay only in a checkout proven to match the certified SHA.

findings.title: Cycle rejection occurs after the edge has already committed

findings.title: WorkGraphs have no enforced freeze boundary
findings.summary: Nodes/edges can be modified while a graph is executable; DAG validation is not tied to a DRAFT→FROZEN lifecycle/hash.
findings.invariant: The implementation must satisfy the stated trust/consistency property on the exact reviewed subject.

evidence.detail: Nodes/edges can be modified while a graph is executable; DAG validation is not tied to a DRAFT→FROZEN lifecycle/hash.

findings.remediation: Add graph DRAFT→FROZEN→RUNNING→terminal state, structure hash, and reject mutation after freeze.
